primary_task: Send a user's deep-research question to a running NVIDIA AI-Q Blueprint backend through scripts/aiq.py (health, chat, research_poll) and present the returned report with citations intact.

requirements.name: python3
requirements.basis: bash: "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts" (python3 is standard on Linux; a newer version is obtainable from Ubuntu apt)

requirements.name: aiq-blueprint-backend
requirements.evidence: A reachable local or self-hosted AI-Q Blueprint backend. / This skill requires a running AI-Q backend; it does not deploy one. / Run `health` before sending research requests.
requirements.basis: lacks: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA"; lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, SaaS products, model hubs, app stores, email delivery, payment)". The manifest lists no AI-Q backend among its tools or grants; a self-hosted backend host is outside the allow-list, and no backend runs at localhost:8000 in a fresh session.

requirements.name: localhost:8000
requirements.evidence: permissions: network: - http://localhost:8000 / network access to a running local AI-Q Blueprint server at `http://localhost:8000` by default
requirements.basis: grants: "local_servers"; bash: "start and stop local servers inside the session" (the network path to localhost exists; what is missing is the server itself, see aiq-blueprint-backend)

notes: Reading taken: the document requires an already-running AI-Q backend and says it does not deploy one; in this runtime no such backend exists and any self-hosted (non-local) backend URL is outside the egress allow-list, so the hard requirement is unavailable. Other reading: if a local AI-Q backend could be deployed inside the session first (the document hands that to a separate skill, aiq-deploy, which is not part of this document), the backend status would be unknown and the verdict ACHIEVABLE; that would need a check that AI-Q can run without Docker or GPU and without NVIDIA-hosted model endpoints (NVIDIA hosts are refused) or model-provider credentials (the manifest has none). Optional follow-ups (report_edit, artifacts download, report --out-dir) are not part of the primary task.
